object.label: H1c — the price leg read by the vote, from the RP corner's hawk, four days on (β, the visible page only): the office's post of 11-04 carried with its fourth condition — 'change our relationship to Israel' — and the house's son endorsing every word; the split in the ticket read from inside the right as the office turning the holder's strategy into 'a liability inside his own political coalition'. The war's cost conceded in the hawk's idiom: a short decisive war 'might have' reconciled the holder's two camps, Iran's sustained missile and drone fire has prolonged it and 'imposed costs American power cannot quickly eliminate', and the measures the objectives need are the ones the restrainers oppose. The pump, the price and the gate are not on the visible page; the vote is there only as the post's occasion

zAxis.pos: the war did not cost the vote and the holder should hold course — the hawk's reading; the war can still be won on the traditionalists' terms
zAxis.neg: the war cost the vote and the holder must end it on the office's four conditions — the restrainers' reading; the costs cannot be eliminated

object.gear: the vote (the post's occasion) and the war itself (its direction, its costs); nothing on the pump, the barrel or the dollar on the visible page

transformNote: the holder's promise is not on the visible page. What is on it is the office's post, carried in full for the first time on the Press — four conditions, the fourth Israel — and an author from the hawk's chair reading it as a liability the office created rather than a cost the war did. The shadow is the hed's question: whether the boss 'agrees' makes the war's direction a matter of the holder's choice between his deputy and his hawks, and leaves the vote's verdict as the deputy's opinion. Before the wall the author concedes the cost in his own idiom (prolonged; costs not quickly eliminated) and then names the cure as the measures the restrainers oppose
